key_findings.finding: Checked all 60 expected answers against the assigned booklet. No material factual contradiction found. In particular, the inspected diagrams support Q39-Q41; Q20 correctly excludes characters from the first tiebreaker; Q34 correctly limits Camaraderie to retreat after combat.

Ledger passes 17 and 18 correctly reject more unit-eligibility examples and routine handling. Their no-addition conclusion is too broad: the controlled-Mill ability and resource-only control branch are substantive rules, not new numbers, alternate routes or star/Factory combinations.

proposed_additions.question: While you control the territory containing your Mill, how does it affect the number of territories you may Produce on and the output there, including when no actual worker is present?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: The Mill territory may count as an extra bonus territory in addition to the normal territories selected for Produce. The Mill produces as if it were one worker, so it can produce even with no actual worker there. Any actual workers on its territory may also produce.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p18, MILL: Whenever you take the Produce action, the territory with the Mill may count as an extra (bonus) territory for production. The Mill will produce as if it were a worker. If there are actual workers on the Mill territory, they may also produce resources.
proposed_additions.novelty: Tests the structure's distinct positive ability: extra eligible territory and worker-equivalent output, including the explicit no-worker consequence. Q11 asks only how Mill and Mine work when enemies occupy their territories; a fully responsive answer can simply say that an uncontrolled Mill cannot Produce. Its key supplies the positive ability without requesting it. Q09 asks the general Produce procedure, with no Mill reference and a key limited to worker production on selected territories. Q26 directly asks Armory/Monument, not Mill. This is not another enemy-control example or changed worker count.
proposed_additions.impact: A player could correctly answer every existing Mill-specific question while omitting the extra territory and mistakenly requiring a real worker for Mill production.

proposed_additions.question: What presence establishes control of a territory, and do resources alone preserve your control after your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: You control a territory with at least one of your units, or with your structure and no enemy units. Resources are not units and do not establish control. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control that territory or the resources left there; those resources cannot be spent by you unless you regain control.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p4, CONTROL: control requires at least one unit or a structure with no enemy units; only one player controls a territory at a time.
Rulebook PDF p4, RESOURCES: resource tokens remain on the board and may be spent only from territories currently controlled.
Rulebook PDF p29, EVERY TERRITORY CONTROLLED and EVERY 2 RESOURCES CONTROLLED; PDF p31, END-GAME SCORING.
proposed_additions.novelty: Tests the source-defined no-qualifying-presence branch and its resource-ownership consequence. Q04 tests an enemy worker on a structure territory and remote spending from already-controlled territories. Q24 tests entry into a structure-only territory. Q20 and Q39 assume territory/resource control while testing scoring. None asks what establishes control or what happens when only resources remain. This follows the explicit control definition rather than introducing a new rule or mechanically combining unrelated abilities.
proposed_additions.impact: A player could answer the existing occupation/capture/payment questions yet incorrectly treat previously produced, unguarded resources as permanently owned and spendable.
